```lean
import CategoryTheory.Limits
import CategoryTheory.Functor
import CategoryTheory.Category
import Fintype

open CategoryTheory

theorem lg_target {G : Type v} [Group G] [Finite G] : 
  CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesColimitsOfShape (CategoryTheory.SingleObj G) FintypeCat.incl := by
  let J := CategoryTheory.SingleObj G
  let F := FintypeCat.incl
  let C := FintypeCat
  let D := Type v

  -- Since G is finite, the category J = SingleObj G is finite
  -- and hence has a well-order. We can use the fact that the inclusion preserves colimits
  -- of shape J if D (the category of types) has colimits of shape J and C (the category of fintypes)
  -- also has colimits of shape J.

  -- First, show that D has colimits of shape J
  have hD : CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimitsOfShape J D := by
    -- The category of types has all colimits, including those of shape J
    -- since J is a finite category (as G is finite)
    exact CategoryTheory.Limits.hasColimitsOfShape_of_finite_shape J

  -- Next, show that C has colimits of shape J
  have hC : CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimitsOfShape J C := by
    -- The category of fintypes has all colimits of shape J
    -- because it is equivalent to the category of finite sets, and J is finite
    exact CategoryTheory.Limits.hasColimitsOfShape_of_finite_shape J

  -- Now apply the evaluation lemma to get that F preserves colimits of shape J
  let l := CategoryTheory.Limits.evaluation_preservesColimitsOfShape J F hC hD
  exact l
```
